chapter: New Orleans dance scene of the 1920s
title: New Orleans bands and cabarets of the golden era, and the Princeton Rebellers
summary: Piron, Kelly, Celestin, Halfway House, the Owls, the Little Club, Scranton Sirens, Tobin, and the little-known Princeton Rebellers with Pinky Vidacovich.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel

blocks.x: Well, I was going to say, just about that time in New Orleans, of course this was, I suppose, the golden era of jazz around this part of the country, because in New Orleans around that time you had bands like, well, of course you had P-Ron out of Tranchina's. You had the old Chris Kelly and the Tuxedo bands, Celestan's band, playing for dancers. You had the Halfway House Band, out of Chris Rabinstein's Halfway House. Well, shortly after that, the Owls at the West End Roof, and the Owls also at the Pontchartrain Rowing Club. Sam Organ was playing here in New Orleans also. You had some fine bands in the cabarets downtown. The Little Club, as an example, hired the best bands that could be found, and even imported some name bands at the time. You might recall hearing one of them on record, which was the Scranton Sirens, which was a band that the Dorses played in. That was probably one of the voice recordings that was actually made in New Orleans. And Johnny Tobin had a band at that time, I think, at the ringside, and he cut the other side of the record, as you recall. There was a good band at the Cadillac Cabaret, but I don't recall the name of it. But there was plenty of good music all around town. Shortly after that, there was a band that played for dances around town. I think very little has been said of. And that was the Princeton Rebellers. Did you ever hear of them?
I have heard of them. I think it was Pinky.

It was a small group with Pinky, Vidalgovich, of course. And it was, as I recall, some of the boys from the Owl Band, because Bill Padron, I think, was on trumpet, and Bert Peck played the piano. I don't recall the rest of them. It was a very fine little band, never recorded, but just played for dances around town.
I think that's a band that combined with the Owls or something.
Probably did, because it was several of the same personnel.
I forget, Pinky told me about it once.
Pinky could give you the story on that, though.
He's one of the ones, isn't he?
